title: I had Claude Code synthesise my web game's music in code: no samples, no licences, a 172 KB seamless loop
author: Commercial_Cable_404
selftext:
Honey Line, my draw-to-protect web puzzle, had no music. Its sound effects were already generated by a Node script, so I asked Claude Code to do the same for a music loop instead of hunting for a licensed track.

The music is data: four chords (Cmaj7, Am7, Fmaj7, G6) at 92 BPM, an 8th-note arpeggio pattern, a sub-bass note per chord and a shaker on every 8th. Each instrument is a small function of time. The marimba is a sine plus a fast-decaying partial at 4x the pitch, and the shaker is differenced noise with a 35 ms decay.

Seamless looping was the fiddly part. Notes are mixed into a circular buffer, so a tail that runs past the end wraps into the start, and the reverb and low-pass filter run two passes for the same reason. No click at the seam.

The script renders three candidate loops in about 1.5 s. Claude can't hear, so it checked what it could by numbers: no clipping, equal loudness across the candidates, and that Chrome decodes the AAC file to exactly the rendered sample count, which is what keeps a WebAudio loop gapless. Then I listened and picked one. The result is a 21 s loop, 172 KB as AAC.

The clip is the promo with that loop plus the game's own sound effects, timed to the animation by reading its timeline from the script that generated it.

The obvious limit: the model can't tell whether it sounds good, so generating a few variants to compare side by side was the most useful part. My next problem is variation, so a 5-minute session doesn't hear the same 21 s fifteen times. Has anyone here done procedural variation for game music beyond simple loops?

Game, free in the browser: [https://playgama.com/game/honey-line](https://playgama.com/game/honey-line)
